messages:
lee (eng-platform): heads up  the "Unit Cost Explorer" sparklines are showing sub-zero amortized costs for some tenant/model combos after today's quota rebind. Screenshot: https://img.redwood/unitcost-neg.png

sasha (sre): weird. Which rollup window and sampling level?

lee (eng-platform): 15m rollup, default sample 1%. affected routes look like ones with heavy prefetch + quota throttles. hypothesis: quota-enforced early rejects removed from denominator but some prefetch tokens still counted as saved, so saved > billed -> negative.

dia (billing): if the UI shows negative $ that's going to confuse finance teams. We should avoid negatives in exported CSVs and invoices. At a minimum, cap at 0 in billing exports.

maya (product-ux): agreed. UX options: (A) clamp to 0 and show small ? info, (B) show an "uncertain range" band (e.g. 0202020to  +X) with a confidence pill, or (C) show raw values behind an "Advanced" toggle. I prefer B.

sam (frontend): B is doable. We can render a translucent positive band and a tooltip that links to diagnostics. Need the API to provide `cache_confidence` & `quota_impact_flag`.

ian (infra): we can add `x-cache-coverage` and `x-prefetch-tokens` to telemetry at the proxy (internal-only headers) and emit to kafka. Example: `x-cache-coverage:0.62`, `x-prefetch-tokens:24`. Non-breaking.

sasha (sre): also we saw an attribution edge: when quota triggers redirect-to-light-sku, the consumer pipeline still credits prefetch savings to the original heavy-sku. quick log excerpt:
```
2026-03-18T10:12:01Z INF route=wallet-sim req_id=xyz primary=redwood-large routed=redwood-small prefetch=18 cached=12
```
That should attribute cached to routed=redwood-small, not primary.

lee (eng-platform): good catch. Current attribution rule is "prefer primary if prefetch present" which was naive. Proposed rule: attribute cache savings to the actually served model (routed) unless the routed model is a fallback due to quota AND prefetch tokens originated from primary in the same invocation window. Need clearer provenance fields.

dia (billing): timeline: billing exports must be stable. Any change to attribution requires a migration plan or dual-run window. We can add a flag `attrib_mode=v2` that produces both old and new columns for 14 days. Then reconcile.

maya (product-ux): product asks for a confidence indicator (high/medium/low) derived from: presence of proxy headers + sample_rate > 0.05 + no quota events. UI copy: "Cache savings (est.) — Confidence: High". Low confidence would show the uncertainty band.

sam (frontend): action items for front-end: 1) clamp export CSV negative values (immediate), 2) render uncertainty band when confidence != high, 3) add toggle to show raw numbers. I'll PR today for (1).

ian (infra): infra tasks: emit headers + kafka keys, add feature flag `emit_cache_provenance` default off. estimate 4h dev + 1h rollout.

sasha (sre): I'll schedule a canary run for the migration and watch query load. Backfill we discussed earlier might be required to reconcile 7 days of history for affected tenants. That will be a separate job.

dia (billing): please include me on the migration RFC and provide a sample of old_vs_new CSV for 3 tenants so we can signoff.

lee (eng-platform): decision summary: 1) immediate: clamp negatives in exports + UI (sam) 2) short-term: add confidence badge and uncertainty band (maya + sam) 3) infra: emit provenance headers + feature flag (ian) 4) data + billing: dual-run attrib_v2 for 14 days and backfill for 7 days as comparison (dia + sasha + ellie to run) 5) roll to canary dashboards next Tue.

costbot: note: scheduled suppression of cost-alerts for tenant-group "alpha" during dual-run window to avoid noisy pages.

lee (eng-platform): created ENGPLAT-7261 with subtasks. tagging @all for quick ack. ping me if anything blocks. :rocket:
